missionDef.name: Corrupted Citadel
missionDef.description: A brutal 7-phase expedition through a citadel overrun with corruption. Three outer waves repeat, two gatekeepers must be overcome, and the final confrontation determines everything. Max 3 total failures before forced withdrawal.

phases.name: Outer Walls — Sweep
phases.description: Clear three waves of corrupted sentinels patrolling the outer wall. Each wave is identical but gets harder.

phases.name: Gatehouse
phases.description: Force the main gate. One chance — failure means regrouping outside.

phases.name: Courtyard Push
phases.description: Advance through the main courtyard under fire. Three sections, each pressed forward regardless of minor failures.

phases.name: The First Keeper

text: The Keeper holds. Waiting on your call.

phases.description: A corrupted lieutenant guards the inner keep. Defeat it or the expedition stalls.

phases.name: The Sanctum Corridor
phases.description: A maze of trapped corridors. Navigate carefully.

phases.name: The Second Keeper

text: Effortless. The corruption had no answer.
The Second Keeper is not done. Your call.

phases.description: The inner sanctum guardian. Far more dangerous than the first. This is your last chance to turn back.

phases.name: The Corruption Source

text: Purged completely. The citadel is free.
The source overwhelms you. Evacuation ordered.
A decisive blow. The source is damaged.

phases.description: The heart of the citadel. One final push — win or lose, there is no going back.

text: Legendary clearance. Songs will be sung.
Perfect execution. The corruption won't return soon.
The expedition collapsed before the inner sanctum.
The citadel is cleansed. A significant victory.

header.title: Season 1: Frost Rising
header.subtitle: The cold winds bring new opportunities.

c.v: Somebody told me there were abandoned GL!TCH-BIO terminals scattered throughout the reconstruction zone.
Then they told me not to mess with them.
Which, if you've never met a PERP before, is a fantastic way to guarantee that I will absolutely mess with them.
Most of these terminals are ancient. Half of them are buried under rubble. The other half are covered in warning labels.
That's how you know they're hiding something useful.
Word is that Dr. Vape left research logs buried inside these systems. If I can recover them, we might learn how the cloning project started.
Or maybe I'll find something even better.
Either way, I'm bringing a screwdriver.

modalDef.name: Mission Complete
modalDef.description: Displayed when a player successfully finishes a mission. Shows rewards earned.

c.v: The rewards have been added to your inventory.
Somebody told me there were abandoned GL!TCH-BIO terminals scattered throughout the reconstruction zone.
Then they told me not to mess with them.
Which, if you've never met a PERP before, is a fantastic way to guarantee that I will absolutely mess with them.
I found references to an incubator.
A real one.
Not theoretical.
Not destroyed.
Still out there somewhere.
Honestly, this mission was a huge success.
And the fact that three security alarms activated during the process is completely unrelated.
